scope: Source review, synthetic native/store seams, actual pinned GGUF header codec and retained p199 token replay only.
checks: Streaming generate/run_turn retain canonical context, append-source identity, pending descriptor, policy and final SAVE/RELEASE gates.
The same front/store objects and parent constructor identity checks are used; no binary/source/admission relaxation is added.
First observer BaseException disables subsequent callback invocations and retains its original object; native parsing and normal disposition continue.
Observer failure does not skip SAVE or final/same-ID RELEASE; native/storage/frame mismatches preserve canonical halt/no-auto-release behavior.
Observation token frames must match native completion exactly; observer error rendering is bounded and guarded.
Incremental decoder uses pinned tokenizer byte mapping and UTF8 replacement, retaining incomplete suffixes until continuation/final flush.
Final canonical decode parity checked; terminal token only suppressed from presentation, retained in full token history; subsequent token refuses.
Real codec tests cover all256 byte pieces, Unicode/subword boundaries, malformed/truncated sequences, nonterminal special tokens and six retained p199 responses.
Exhaustive pinned-vocabulary census confirms maximum128 raw bytes/token;512-token bound limits raw input65536 bytes, worst-case encoded replacement output196608 bytes.
limitations: Observers are trusted bounded local callbacks, not an asynchronous scheduler; they must not block or mutate/reenter the native front/store/engine.
Production identity/admission still belongs to the surrounding coordinator; synthetic engine tests do not qualify native behavior.
Service must consult both observer and delivery failures before final success/DONE; observer completion counts do not prove wire delivery.
No real native/model streaming, integrated SSE endpoint or performance result is established.
